title: Kernel Module Loaded From An Unusual Path
detection_hypothesis: If a kernel-level component is loaded outside package management, the module loading utility will be invoked with a path in a writable directory.

field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.
field_semantics.CommandLine: Full command line including arguments as supplied to the process.

collection_prerequisites: An execve audit rule or equivalent process telemetry agent is deployed.
Audit rules are not limited to a narrow allowlist of binaries.
expected_collection_gaps: Containers without a shared audit namespace may not report execve records.
Audit backlog limits can drop records under load.
normalization_assumptions: Image is the absolute executable path and CommandLine is the joined argument vector.
ParentImage identifies the parent executable path.
ingestion_differences: auditd argument vectors may be hex-encoded before normalization.
Some agents report the argv array instead of a joined string.
retention_considerations: Execve telemetry is high volume; 30 to 60 days of hot retention is typical.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches occur on engineering and diagnostic hosts under a support case. Tune on the host role and require the module to be removed at the end of the session.
tuning_guidance: Exclude engineering hosts by name if necessary. Do not exclude the module loading utilities on production servers.
test_strategy: Positive cases load modules from the temporary and home directories. Negative cases load from the managed module tree, remove a module, and list modules.

attack_techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Kernel Modules and Extensions
